title: fix: make the how-it-works page reachable and add structured data
body:
Diagnosed from the live Search Console for `https://aijobhunter.app/`, not from a checklist.

## The problem

Google indexes **4 of 9 pages**. Absent: `/how-it-works`, `/agent-system`, `/architecture-map`, `/world`, `/accessibility`.

Indexing tracks internal link count almost monotonically:

| Route | Inbound internal links | Indexed |
|---|---|---|
| `/download` | 7 | ✅ |
| `/privacy` | 5 | ✅ |
| `/creature` | 4 | ✅ |
| `/accessibility` | 3 | ❌ |
| `/world`, `/architecture-map`, `/agent-system` | 1 each | ❌ |
| `/how-it-works` | **0** | ❌ |

`/how-it-works` had **no `<a href="/how-it-works">` anywhere on the site**. Every other occurrence of the string is a stylesheet name, a test, a comment, or `<code>` prose. The most commercially useful page was unreachable by crawl, while a doodle short film and the privacy policy were indexed.

Compounding it, the sitemap had **never been read** — Search Console listed zero submitted or discovered sitemaps, even though `robots.ts` correctly declares it and #922 ships the file. Declaring a sitemap in `robots.txt` is evidently not sufficient. It has now been submitted manually, so the orphans will be discovered regardless; internal links still matter for crawl priority and link equity.

For context on why this matters: 3 months of traffic is **84 impressions, 2 clicks, average position 39.1**, and all 12 queries are brand-navigational. Nothing in the index answers a question anyone searches.

## Changes

- `/how-it-works` now appears in the shared footer, the homepage's own footer row, and one descriptive in-content hero link. `/agent-system` and `/architecture-map` gain footer links.
- `SoftwareApplication` JSON-LD on the homepage — the site had **no** structured data. No `aggregateRating`: there are no real reviews, and inventing one is both a Google penalty and a lie.
- Titles carry a searchable phrase; the joke moves to `openGraph.title`, which is what people actually see when a link is shared.
- The six pages that declared no `openGraph.images` now reuse the existing card.

### Titles changed — easy to veto

| Page | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `/` | `AI Job Hunter — please hire him` | `AI Job Hunter — Job Search, Résumé & Cover Letters` |
| `/how-it-works` | `— How It Works (End to End)` | `— How It Works, Step by Step` |
| `/download` | `— Download` | `— Download for macOS, Windows, Linux` |

`/creature` untouched — it is a standalone creative piece.

## Not fixed, deliberately

The 4 URLs reporting *"not indexed / Alternate page with proper canonical tag"* are `/index.html`, `/download.html`, `?ref=producthunt` and `?ref=launches.uicomet.com` — correct canonicalization working as intended, not a defect.

## Verification

`pnpm --filter @ajh/landing test` 326 passed · `build` emits all 14 static pages · `check:parity` OK (27 signature phrases, 13 legacy links, 7 installer URLs) · `typecheck` · `lint:strict` clean.

`SiteFooter.test.tsx`, `HowItWorksBody.test.tsx` and `scripts/check-parity.mjs` were updated alongside — each asserts exact footer text or a frozen title phrase, and each exists to catch a silently-dropped link, so their intent is preserved rather than loosened.

title: feat: offer reasoning effort per model and fix embedding re-indexing
body:
Two AI-provider fixes that share the adapter files, so they ship together.

## Re-indexing reported success while writing nothing

Input was truncated to a fixed character budget that overflows a dense language's token window, every provider error was swallowed, and the batch completed regardless — so the status strip correctly read `0/1 indexed` underneath two success toasts.

Input is now chunked and mean-pooled so the whole document is embedded, the working chunk size is learned once per document and bounded, and a run that embeds nothing fails instead of reporting success. Gemini's default embedding model had been **retired by Google in January**; changing the code default fixed nothing because the resolved name is persisted, so a migration rewrites it and evicts the caches keyed on it.

## Reasoning effort reached only the Codex agent

Every HTTP adapter dropped the setting. It is now gated on the per-model reasoning capability, and the levels a picker offers come from the backend **per model** — providers publish different vocabularies per model, and an unsupported value is rejected outright.

## ⚠️ One-time effect on first launch

Stored vectors carry a format version, and this bumps it. Vectors written before this change were truncated-prefix embeddings and are **not comparable** with pooled ones, so every stored vector reads stale and lazily re-embeds. Nothing unrecoverable is deleted — only regenerable caches (`posting_vectors`, `match_scores`). This is intended and one-way.

## Review notes

A security gate plus a three-pass review ensemble ran before this opened. Findings worth calling out, because each needed the code executed rather than read:

- **The learned chunk size was poisoned by each chunk's leftover tail**, so one short remainder shrank the working size for the rest of the document. A 300,000-character résumé burned its entire call budget and failed after embedding 3% of its text. Fixed; the same document now completes in 97 calls.
- **Gemini's per-model level table was built, tested and advertised to the UI, but never consulted on the send path.** Since the setting is stored per *provider*, switching Gemini models carried a level the new model rejects straight to the API.
- **The spend ledger recorded nothing when a multi-chunk embed failed partway**, discarding calls already billed — a regression introduced by moving the paid call inside a retry loop.
- **This branch had added a model to the one-click list that Google has since shut down.** All three stale-model defects here came from hardcoded lists that were correct when written, so each such list now records the vendor page it was checked against and the date.

The adaptive embedding path moved to its own module: adding it had nearly doubled the provider module, tripping the architecture LOC rule. Split rather than allowlisted — the rule exists to report exactly that.

title: fix: warn when local ollama has no account key for company research
body:
Company research on local Ollama needs a free Ollama **account key** (credential slot `ollama-cloud`), because Ollama has no model-side web search — the app calls its web search API instead. Without the key the backend returns nothing and the renderer swallows the failure, so a missing key looked exactly like *"found nothing"*, and the cover letter was generated ungrounded with no signal to the user.

## What changed

The interview-questions modal already warned about this, and the AI-Generate fine-tune step carried its own guarded copy of the same rule. Both now consume one shared hook, and the hint appears beside the "research company" toggle in the tailor flow too. No new strings — the existing translation is reused.

## Review notes

The pre-PR review caught that the repo had **two** implementations of this predicate, and the first attempt at consolidation extracted the wrong one — dropping a cold-boot guard added by #682. Both defaults fail *into* the hint (`activeProvider` defaults to `ollama` before the config resolves, `has` defaults to `false` before the key query resolves), so an unguarded check tells a user who **already has** the key that they need to add it, on first paint of a cold session. Reproduced by executing the hook against a stub client.

The shared hook now guards both pending windows — including the key-query one, which the fine-tune copy never covered — and the fine-tune step was migrated, so there is genuinely one predicate in one place rather than two.

The hint is announced (`role="status"`, `aria-live="polite"`): the provider picker sits directly above it, so switching providers makes it appear in response to the user's own action, and `TailorWizard` has no ambient live region the way its sibling wizards do.

Tests were tightened alongside: the a11y attributes are now asserted by role rather than text (stripping them fails the suite), and the credential-slot argument is asserted rather than discarded by the mock — previously, changing `ollama-cloud` to `ollama` would have kept every test green while pinning the hint on for every Ollama user in production.

title: fix: keep project links out of the resume header and make them work
body:
Fixes three defects reported from one generated résumé.

## Project URLs rendered on the contact line

Project sites were swept into the contact profile's extra links at import, so the exported header rendered them on the contact line **and** again in PROJECTS. Only platform profiles may seed extra links now, and website selection prefers an apex over its own subdomains, so it no longer depends on the order links happen to appear in the source PDF.

## PROJECTS read as `Name — same-name-slug`, with no links

The prompt asked for that shape, and link injection matched the machine label literally while the PDF extractor humanised it differently — so the label never matched and nothing linked. Items now carry their real name; matching is normalised and assigns each link to its best line; job-board and non-personal profile URLs are dropped rather than becoming invented projects; and a link that still matches nothing is placed in the localized projects section or left unplaced, never appended as an orphan.

## The header in the editor differed from the exported one

Edits to it were silently discarded from PDF and DOCX while still shipping in TXT and clipboard copy. The document text now owns the header at export; the profile seeds it at generation and fills only what the text leaves blank. See [ADR-0021](docs/adr/0021-editor-owns-resume-header.md).

## Review notes

This went through three security rounds and a three-pass review ensemble before opening. Findings worth calling out, because each was invisible in the diff and only appeared when a reviewer executed the code:

- The header-seeding scan could **delete résumé content** — an entire job, a skills line, a project link — for four of the seven locales the app generates for, and for English résumés whose first heading wasn't in the recognised list. Seeding now only ever replaces one line or inserts; removal is structurally impossible.
- The Resume Builder path was never seeded, so making export fallback-only would have shipped the model's invented contact line. Both generation paths now seed through one helper, and the prompt's false promise that the line "will be replaced on export" is gone.
- A profile with only a name never seeded it, and export could not rescue it.
- The two profile lookups were unguarded and could discard a completed, already-paid-for generation.

Rules that exist in both Rust and TypeScript are now gated by shared JSON fixtures asserted from both sides, and the section-name list is read from its fixture by TypeScript rather than duplicated — after three separate bugs this session traced to a mirrored rule whose comment claimed a parity it did not have.

title: fix: upload only our own debug files to sentry
body:
Found by inspecting the first real release run ([30741386889](https://github.com/saeedkolivand/ai-job-hunter-app/actions/runs/30741386889)).

## The good news first

Everything from #927/#929 worked on all four matrix legs: symbol upload `success`, flag step correctly `skipped`, assets published before symbols, no cascade into the updater jobs, `Created release 0.132.0`. **The auth token is valid** — that was the one thing tests could not prove.

## The bug

```
> Uploaded 474 missing debug information files
```

Per leg. ~1900 per release. What actually went up:

```
release/build/aws-lc-sys-.../out/chacha20_poly1305_x86_64.o
release/build/proc-macro2-.../build-script-build
release/deps/libscroll_derive-....so
AI Job Hunter.AppDir/usr/lib/libicudata.so.70
AI Job Hunter.AppDir/usr/lib/libudev.so.1
AI Job Hunter.AppDir/usr/bin/ajh-tauri          ← the only one that matters
```

Dependency build scripts, proc-macro `.so`s, `ring`/`aws-lc-sys` object files, and the third-party system libraries bundled into the AppImage. I had pointed `sentry-cli debug-files upload` at the whole `target/` tree.

## The fix, and why it is derived rather than guessed

Scoped to `ajh_tauri*` under `release/deps`. I took the paths **from that run's logs instead of inferring them**, which turned out to matter — my first attempt at this patch guessed `target/<triple>/release/ajh-tauri.dSYM` and would have been wrong on two platforms:

| Platform | Actual |
| --- | --- |
| Linux | `release/deps/ajh_tauri-<hash>` |
| Windows | `release\deps\ajh_tauri.exe` + **`ajh_tauri.pdb`** |
| macOS | `<triple>/release/deps/ajh_tauri-<hash>` + `.dSYM` |

On every platform the artifacts carry the **library** name (`ajh_tauri`, underscore) and sit in `deps/` — not the bin name at `release/ajh-tauri`. The guessed path would have uploaded the macOS binary **with no debug companion**: symbolication silently degraded, which is this feature's signature failure.

The copies under `release/`, `bundle/appimage/` and `bundle/deb/` are hardlinks that dedupe to the same debug id, so nothing is lost by ignoring them.

Also guarded the per-triple directory behind a non-empty check — with `matrix.target` empty the path collapses to `target//release/deps`, the same directory, enumerating everything twice.

## Verification

Simulated all three real layouts plus the empty case:

```
linux   -> 2: deps/ajh_tauri-fa4fa53a  deps/ajh_tauri-fa4fa53a.d
windows -> 2: deps/ajh_tauri.exe       deps/ajh_tauri.pdb
macos   -> 2: <triple>/deps/ajh_tauri-d8c3e74  <triple>/deps/ajh_tauri-d8c3e74.dSYM
empty   -> 0  (fails loudly, per the existing guard)
```

474 → 2 per leg, debug companion included in every case. YAML parses, step body passes `bash -n`, `continue-on-error` untouched (see ADR-0020 for why it must stay).

title: fix: fail the release when a configured sentry symbol upload breaks
body:
The symbol upload was `continue-on-error: true`, so a wrong token or a rejected upload would skip silently — and the first you'd know is a crash report full of unresolved addresses. That is the *same* silent-failure mode this feature was reviewed for three separate times in #927.

Now that the Sentry secrets are actually provisioned, "skip quietly" only makes sense for forks.

## Changes

- **Dropped `continue-on-error`** and added `set -euo pipefail`, so any failure past the secrets guard turns the run red.
- **Moved the step after `Upload Release Assets`.** The installers are published first, so a Sentry outage or an expired token never costs a release — but the run still fails visibly afterwards. Symbols associate by debug-id, not by upload order, so nothing is lost by uploading second.
- **Absent secrets remain a legitimate skip** (a fork, or a release cut before provisioning), now emitted as a `::warning::` annotation rather than a plain log line — so **"not configured" stays distinguishable from "configured wrong"**, which is the distinction that was collapsed before.

## Verification

Parsed the workflow and asserted the invariants rather than eyeballing them:

```
YAML parses OK
assets step index: 19 | symbols step index: 20
ORDER OK: symbols upload after assets
continue-on-error: (absent - fails loudly)
```

ADR-0020 records the trade-off under Consequences.

## Note

This makes a *configured-but-broken* pipeline loud, which is the point. It cannot make the first release pass or fail on its own — whether the pasted token value is correct is still only knowable from that first run, where Sentry's "Last access" column flips from *never used*.

title: feat: add opt-out crash reporting via sentry
body:
Adds remote crash reporting to the desktop app. Plan: `.claude/plans/polished-singing-graham.md`, decision recorded in **ADR-0020**.

**This reverses a published promise.** The privacy policy named Sentry, by name, as absent in three places, and ADR-0005 defined the local-first guarantee as "no telemetry". That was a deliberate product decision by the owner, not an oversight — the docs are rewritten here in the same PR because `check:parity` and `check:landing-drift` fail if code and copy disagree.

## Why

The app was blind in production. The panic hook wrote `crashes.log` and the diagnostics zip could export it, but both required the user to notice a failure, find the export, and file an issue by hand. React errors caught by a boundary never reached `window` at all, so they were invisible even in principle.

## Scope

Desktop app **only**. The extension keeps its AMO `data_collection_permissions: ['none']` declaration true, and the landing site keeps its no-third-party-JS origin invariant (a foreign script there could read the mission-control PAT from `localStorage`).

## The four things that make "default ON" defensible

1. **Consent gate.** Transmission requires `enabled && consentShown`, not just `enabled`. The default is on, but nothing is sent until the setup wizard has actually shown the choice. A user who never finishes onboarding never reports anything — failing closed.
2. **Redaction.** Every event is serialized, every string passed through the same `redact_token` pipeline the diagnostics bundle uses (ADR-027), then deserialized. Whole-event rather than field-by-field, because a field list is a denylist that rots as the SDK adds fields. `send_default_pii` off; `server_name` overridden (the SDK otherwise sends the machine hostname, often the owner's real name).
3. **No DSN outside release.** `build.rs` bakes it from an env var set only in the signed release job, read via `option_env!`. Local builds, contributor clones and every CI check compile to `None` and cannot transmit.
4. **Extension excluded**, as above.

## Notable implementation decisions

- **Consent is Rust-owned, not a renderer preference.** `sentry::init` must run before `tauri::Builder` because `sentry-rust-minidump` forks the crash-reporter process at startup and `panic = "abort"` leaves nothing in-process able to flush a crash. There is no WebView that early, so no `localStorage` — hence a small JSON file plus an IPC pair.
- **No CSP change.** The plugin's browser side uses a custom transport that forwards WebView events to the Rust SDK over `invoke`, so the renderer never egresses. Widening `connect-src` is rated HIGH/CRITICAL in this repo; it stays untouched.
- **`sentry` is pinned to 0.42, not 0.49.** `tauri-plugin-sentry` 0.5 (the latest) builds against 0.42; a newer `sentry` links a second, type-incompatible copy and `init(&client)` stops accepting our client.
- **No hand-rolled `window.onerror`.** The injected browser SDK already installs global handlers; a second listener would double-report. Only React 19's `onCaughtError` is wired, because boundary-caught errors never reach `window`.
- **Release profile now keeps symbols** (`debug = "line-tables-only"`, `split-debuginfo = "packed"`, `strip = "debuginfo"`) and CI uploads sidecars to Sentry — never attached to the release, since full DWARF for this dep tree is large.

## Docs rewritten

All twelve claim sites, plus ADR-0005 (eighth egress class) and new ADR-0020. Two worth calling out:

- **`Footer.tsx`** claimed *"Because there's no server-side copy, deleting locally deletes it everywhere"* — flatly false once reports exist. Replaced with the erasure path.
- **`/privacy` is the policy URL filed with both Chrome Web Store and Firefox AMO.** It now states desktop collection and extension non-collection as separate sections, so a reviewer cannot read one as the other while the manifest still declares `['none']`.

## Verification

`cargo test --lib` (5 new crash_reporting tests incl. the redaction gate) · `cargo test --test architecture` · `cargo clippy --all-features` · `cargo fmt --check` · `pnpm test` 4636 passed · `pnpm typecheck` · `pnpm lint` · `check:parity` against a fresh landing build · `check:landing-drift` · pre-push gate incl. cargo-deny and cargo-machete.

Claim sweep (`rg -i "no telemetry|no analytics|phones home|No Sentry"`) returns only extension-scoped hits and historical commit data.

## Known limitations, stated not hidden

- Turning reporting off unbinds the client immediately, but the minidump supervisor is a separate process forked at launch and only stops at restart. The settings copy says so.
- **5k errors/month is a quota on errors, not users.** One crash loop can exhaust it in a day. Worth setting a client `sample_rate` and per-issue server-side rate limiting before the user base grows — noted in ADR-0020, not done here.

## Needs before this actually reports

Three repo secrets: `AJH_SENTRY_DSN`, `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`, `SENTRY_ORG`, `SENTRY_PROJECT`. Without them the build compiles inert and the symbol-upload step skips itself — nothing breaks.

title: fix: bump the privacy policy last-updated date and centralize it
body:
Follow-up to #927. I rewrote what `/privacy` says the app collects and left **`Last updated: 30 June 2026`** untouched.

That page is the privacy-policy URL filed with **both** the Chrome Web Store and Firefox AMO. A stale date there isn't cosmetic — it asserts a review that predates the change it describes, on a document store reviewers read against the code.

## Fix

Bumped to **2 August 2026**, and moved it into a single exported `LAST_UPDATED` constant in `sections/Footer.tsx`, right next to the "we'll bump the date" promise it backs. That mirrors `components/accessibility/sections/Footer.tsx`, which already had this shape — the privacy page was the odd one out, hardcoding the date in a different file from the promise about it.

Added a test pinning that the page renders the constant in `D Month YYYY` form, so a hardcoded date can't creep back in.

## What the test deliberately does not claim

The accessibility page enforces a 12-month staleness cutoff because it *promises* annual review. The privacy page promises something different — "if this policy changes, we'll bump the date" — which is change-triggered, not cadence-based. Nothing mechanical ties a copy edit to a date bump, so I didn't fake a guard that would either fail spuriously after 12 quiet months or give false confidence. - **Stop hook → deterministic Tier-0 only** (ast-grep arch guards + ledger re-emits + reviewed-hash cache, ~1.3s, hook timeout 130s→30s). Unresolved ledger findings still re-block a finish.

title: docs: consolidate 13 agent rule files into a canonical agents.md
body:
## Why

The repo maintained **13 hand-written copies of the same coding rules** — and they had already drifted:

- **`NumberField`**, a primitive named in enforced rule 5, existed in `CLAUDE.md` alone. The other twelve files taught a stale primitive set.
- **`apps/landing`**, a whole workspace with its own row in the ownership table, existed in `CLAUDE.md` alone.
- `CLAUDE.md` was ~10h ahead of the rest, and every rule change meant 13 edits with nothing enforcing the 13th.

This is the exact failure the Claude Code docs warn about: *"if two rules contradict each other, Claude may pick one arbitrarily."*

## What changed

`AGENTS.md` becomes canonical — the [Linux Foundation standard](https://agents.md/), read natively by Copilot, Cursor, Windsurf and Codex. `CLAUDE.md` imports it via the [documented `@AGENTS.md` pattern](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory) and keeps only Claude-Code-specific orchestration (subagent fleet, review gates, model tiering) — none of which other tools can act on.

| File | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `AGENTS.md` | canonical rules, all 16 enforced rules verbatim |
| `CLAUDE.md` | `@AGENTS.md` + Claude-only layer, 57 lines |
| `.clinerules`, `.codexrules`, `.roorules`, `.jba/guidelines.md`, `.aider/system-prompt.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md` | one-line pointers |
| `.windsurfrules`, `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` (4) | deleted — read `AGENTS.md` natively |

**−1,398 / +101 lines.** Combined always-loaded context is 136 lines, inside Anthropic's documented 200-line target.

Trim pass applied while merging (the `/doctor` heuristic): cut what an agent can derive from the codebase — the package-layout block, name-to-path lookup rows — kept every enforced rule verbatim plus the non-obvious locations (`SCRAPERS` registry, Rust centralized layers, design/motion tokens).

## Mechanical enforcement, not discipline

`pnpm check:agent-system` Check 7 is inverted and tightened: tool files must name `AGENTS.md` **and stay under 1KB**, so re-forking a ruleset fails pre-push and CI rather than rotting silently. Running it is what surfaced the four rule files beyond the nine originally counted.

Drive-by: `.aider.conf.yml` pointed at `packages/shared/src/ipc/contracts.ts`, removed long ago.

## Verification

- `pnpm check:agent-system` ✅ green
- All **16** enforced rules survive the merge (16 before, 16 after — counted against `HEAD~1`)
- `@AGENTS.md` on line 1, unfenced, verified intact after prettier ran via lint-staged
- `eslint scripts/check-agent-system.mjs` ✅ clean
- Reviewer check: run `/context` in a fresh session and confirm **Memory files** lists both `CLAUDE.md` and the expanded `AGENTS.md`

Updates `lint-staged` from 17.1.0 to 17.2.0
Release notes

Sourced from lint-staged's releases.

v17.2.0

Minor Changes

  • #1823 ee156cc - The chunking of tasks based on maximum command line argument length has been re-implemented to be more precise. Now the chunking happens based on the final generated command string, instead of just the list of staged files like previously. This benefits mainly Windows platforms and function commands like:

    /** @type {import('lint-staged').Configuration} */
export default {
  "*.ts": () => "tsc", // Run "tsc" when any TS file is changed (for entire project)
};

    Where the spawned command is literally "tsc" without any extra arguments. Previously, this was still chunked when a lot of files were staged. Now, it probably won't be chunked because the length of the command is just three letters.

    Also, native JavaScript/Node.js function tasks won't be chunked at all, when previously they were run multiple times when chunked:

    /** @type {import('lint-staged').Configuration} */
export default {
  "*.js": {

## What

`MissionControl.tsx` was **701 lines** mixing GitHub data loading, view-model assembly, formatters, and five page sections in one file. This is PR 1 of 4 splitting the oversized `apps/landing` components.

**Pure logic → `lib/mission-control/model.ts`**, joining the eight already-tested modules in that directory:

- `safe`, `loadAll`
- `buildModel` + `type Model` — 66 lines of pure `RepoData → Model` with zero React

**Markup → components**, collapsing the repeated shapes to one definition each:

`MissionControl.tsx` now holds state, the four effects, `confirm`/`runAction`, the three `useMemo`s and composition — **235 lines**.

## Behavior

title: refactor: split agent-fleet into sections and pure scroll modules
body:
## What

`AgentFleet.tsx` was **830 lines**: six page sections, three scroll-driven effects, and a component defined inside the render body. PR 3 of 4 splitting the oversized `apps/landing` components.

**Pure math → `lib/agent-system/`:** `links.ts` (bezier geometry), `belt.ts` (scrub progress, `activeX` interpolation, nearest-station argmin), `reveal.ts` (count-up cubic easing, scene clamp), `clipboard.ts` (copy helper + the Enter/Space `onKeyDown` that was duplicated on both `.copy-cmd` buttons), `constants.ts`.

The hardcoded `/ 9` at three sites is now `STATION_COUNT`, derived from `STATIONS.length`. The `(max-width:780px)` breakpoint, the 160ms resize debounce, the 900ms count duration, the 1300ms copied timeout and the IO thresholds are named constants instead of bare literals.

**Effects → `hooks.ts`:** `useMapLinks`, `useBeltScrub`, `useReveal`, each keeping its own rAF ticking flag and listener teardown.

**Markup → components:** six `sections/*Section.tsx`, plus `Glyph`, `Machine`, `Divider` (6 render sites), `Station` (one component rendering both the `.belt` and `.belt-vert` DOM shapes) and `NodeButton`. Hero coords, the six divider paths, legend rows, the three team lists and the save-job prompt move to `data/agent-fleet.ts` as **additive** exports — `AgentTuple`/`AUTHORS`/`PAIRS`/`CROSS_NODES`/`ROUTES`/`STATIONS`/`BY_NAME` are untouched, and `scripts/check-agent-system.mjs` still passes.

`AgentFleet.tsx` is now **29 lines**.

## The one behavior change

**`NodeButton` is hoisted from the render body to module scope.** It previously got a fresh component identity on every render, so React unmounted and remounted it — focus and CSS transitions restarted. It now takes `{ name, roleClass, selected, onSelect, onHover }`, with the three call sites passing `selected === name`, `setSelected` and `setLitName` explicitly. Everything else in this PR is behavior-preserving.

Beyond the plan, state also follows its markup: `route` into `IntakeSection`, `selected`/`litName` into `FleetMapSection`, with `useMapLinks`/`useBeltScrub` called from the sections that own their DOM. Only `useReveal` stays at the root, since `.reveal`/`.draw` spans every section. That is why the root landed at 29 lines instead of the planned ~120, with no prop drilling.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @ajh/landing typecheck` — clean
- `pnpm --filter @ajh/landing test` — 167 tests, 21 files, all pass
- `pnpm lint:strict` — clean at `--max-warnings 0`
- `pnpm exec prettier --check` — clean
- `node scripts/check-agent-system.mjs` — in sync

## What

#915 and #916 pulled geometry, scroll and easing math out of `ArchitectureMap` and `AgentFleet` into pure modules **specifically so it could be tested**, then deferred the tests. This pays that back — the last of the three follow-ups from that batch.

**90 new cases** across six co-located test files:

| Module | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| `lib/agent-system/belt.ts` | `STATION_COUNT` invariant, `beltProgress` clamp table, `activeStationX` interpolation, `nearestStationIndex` |
| `lib/agent-system/links.ts` | `linkPathD` anchors, cubic control-point structure, degenerate rects |
| `lib/agent-system/reveal.ts` | `easeOutCubic`, `sceneProgress`, `countUp` (both the reduced-motion sync path and the animated one) |
| `lib/agent-system/clipboard.ts` | `copyChip` precedence + timer, `copyChipOnKeyDown` key filtering |
| `lib/architecture-map/geometry.ts` | `edgePath`, `fit`, `screenToVB`, `stageCenter`, `zoomAt`, `ensureVisible` |
| `lib/architecture-map/filter.ts` | `buildAdjacency`, `hasBadge`, `passNodeFilter`, `passEdgeFilter` |

The cases target **boundaries, not happy paths**: zoom clamped at, below and above `ZOOM_MIN`/`ZOOM_MAX`; `easeOutCubic` checked for *deceleration* by comparing deltas across the domain rather than just pinning endpoints; `screenToVB` round-tripped against its forward transform; `nearestStationIndex` swept for a valid index on every input including ±Infinity; `copyChip` driven through the `.copied` timer with fake timers; `edgePath` asserted structurally rather than by brittle full-string match on the `d`.

Landing suite: **167 → 257 tests**.

## Two source quirks documented, not fixed

Both asserted with explanatory comments rather than silently patched, since this is a test-only change:

- `sceneProgress(0, 0, 0)` returns `NaN` — `0/0` escapes both clamp comparisons, because `NaN < 0` and `NaN > 1` are each `false`. Needs a simultaneously zero-height scene *and* viewport, which a real `getBoundingClientRect` never produces.
- `nearestStationIndex([], x)` returns `0`, an invalid index for an empty array. `centers` derives from `STATIONS`, which is never empty.

Neither is reachable through the real callers. A one-line guard on each (`Number.isFinite` clamp, `-1` sentinel) is cheap hardening if you want it — say the word and it's a fast-follow.

`test` (257 pass) · `typecheck` · `lint:strict` · `prettier --check` — all clean.

`testing-reviewer` audited and found nothing blocking. It specifically attacked the risk that geometry tests just restate the source formula: it hand-mutated a sign flip into `zoomAt`'s pan term and traced the assertions through, confirming they fail against the broken implementation. It also verified the RAF stub in `reveal.test.ts` drives three explicit frames deterministically rather than firing once, and confirmed `git diff` touches **no production code**.

body:
## What

The landing site shipped with no crawl metadata at all — no `robots.txt`, no sitemap, and nothing aimed at LLM crawlers. This adds all three.

- **`src/app/robots.ts`** — allows everything except `/mission-control` (a live GitHub-API dashboard that already sets `robots: { index: false }` in its page metadata; this repeats it at the crawl layer so bots skip the fetch), and points at the sitemap.
- **`src/app/sitemap.ts`** — the 8 indexable routes, each matching that page's own `alternates.canonical`. No `lastModified`/`priority`: Google ignores priority outright, and a build-time timestamp would churn the file on every deploy.
- **`public/llms.txt`** — follows the llms.txt convention (H1, `>` summary, key facts, `## Pages`, `## Optional`). `/world` and `/creature` sit under Optional since they are visual and carry no facts a crawler needs.

## Why llms.txt, given adoption is unproven

No major AI crawler has committed to reading `llms.txt`, and the bots that do hit us (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot) crawl HTML and obey `robots.txt`. It is included anyway because the file is static, costs one bullet per new page, and pays off if adoption lands. `robots.txt` and the sitemap are the parts that actually get read today.

## Gotcha worth remembering

Next 16 metadata routes default to **dynamic**, and `output: 'export'` hard-errors on them (`export const dynamic = "force-static" ... not configured on route "/robots.txt"`). Both files need `export const dynamic = 'force-static'`. Commented in place.

## Verification

- `pnpm typecheck` — pass

body:
## Why

`.github/workflows/claude-review.yml` has always told Claude to *"Post findings as inline comments on the changed lines"* in both lanes. **Neither lane could.** The instruction was a silent no-op — findings landed in the tag-mode tracking comment (Lane A1) or only in the sticky comment (Lane A2).

Ported from the same fix in [`crosskit#66`](https://github.com/saeedkolivand/crosskit/pull/66), verified against the action source at the SHA this repo already pins (`be7b93b1` = v1.0.183):

- The inline-comment MCP server starts **only** when `allowedTools` contains a `mcp__github_inline_comment__`-prefixed entry — `src/mcp/install-mcp-server.ts:80,138-142`.
- Tag mode's own list is `Glob, Grep, LS, Read, mcp__github_comment__update_claude_comment, mcp__github_ci__*` — `src/modes/tag/index.ts:123-133`. No inline tool.
- Agent mode passes `parseAllowedTools(claude_args)` to the **same** check (`src/modes/agent/index.ts`), and `pull_request` is an entity event with `isPR: true` (`src/github/context.ts:191-201`) — so the automatic gate can post inline too.

So the workflow's two explanatory comments were both wrong: tag mode does *not* grant the tools, and a `prompt` does *not* deny them. Naming the tool is the whole fix.

## What changed

| --- | --- |

title: feat: add an accessibility statement and fix the barriers it found
body:
Adds `/accessibility` — a [WAI-model](https://www.w3.org/WAI/planning/statements/) accessibility statement covering the landing site, the desktop app and the browser extension — **and fixes every WCAG A/AA violation it found**.

## Why, and why it doesn't overclaim

Publishing this isn't legally required here — the EAA's microenterprise exemption covers a solo maintainer's free service, and no US statute requires one from a private site. It ships because this is a job-hunting tool whose users include disabled job seekers, and because a false "fully conformant" claim would be worse than no page at all.

So every claim on the page traces to a measured result, not boilerplate.

## What the audit found, and what it is now

axe-core 4.12 (WCAG 2.0/2.1/2.2 A+AA tags) against the **built** `out/`, plus a scripted keyboard tab-through:

| surface | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| landing, 9 pages | 3 serious rules | **0** |
| desktop home view | 1 critical + 1 serious, 12 nodes | **0**, both colour schemes |

**Landing fixes**

- `/creature` — the faded doodle annotations diluted `--ink` toward the paper background via opacity. Now an explicit warm grey at **4.98:1**, up from 2.46–2.8:1.
- `/world` — the active nav pill darkens its accent with `color-mix`. White on the darkened red is **8.54:1**, up from 3.93:1. The accent cycles per section, and the **blue** state was **1.88:1** — a worse failure the original single-state scan never saw, now 4.86:1. Found by reading the code, not by scanning.
- `/architecture-map` — the sidebar is keyboard-reachable and named. The map's window-level arrow-key pan handler now excludes it, so arrows scroll the sidebar instead of panning the map underneath it. Verified in a browser (focus lands on `#side`, ArrowDown moves `scrollTop` 0 → 80) and covered by a new test that fails against the pre-fix code.

**Desktop fixes**

- The critical `aria-allowed-attr` was `aria-expanded` on a roleless wrapper `div` in the shared `packages/ui` `HoverPopover`. The invalid attribute is now gone from that wrapper everywhere the component is used, and moves onto the trigger where the trigger is a real button — so this cleared the same latent defect at every call site, not just the home view.
- The 11 contrast failures use the existing `text-muted-foreground` token (5.1:1 on white, 4.8:1 on `#f8f8f8`, clear in dark too) instead of low-alpha `text-foreground/30|40|55`.

## What the statement still discloses

Zero automated violations is **not** conformance, so both surfaces stay **partially conformant** and the extension stays **not assessed**. The page states plainly that:

- **the contrast fix is scoped to the home view** — ~460 of the renderer's ~1,100 `text-foreground/NN` usages sit at sub-AA steps, and no other view has been scanned. A global migration is a wide visual diff that needs its own PR and a Lost Pixel review;
- two `best-practice` rules remain on the home view (`landmark-unique`, `region`) — outside WCAG A/AA, but known;
- the three CI a11y gates are **advisory, not blocking**;
- exported PDFs are **not tagged to PDF/UA-1**;
- automated tooling catches roughly a third of WCAG issues, there has been **no third-party audit**, and **no testing with assistive-technology users**.

## The statement page itself

axe 0 violations · 24/24 tab stops with a visible ring · `H1` + 9×`H2`, no skipped levels, no duplicate ids · anchors reveal on focus · no overflow at 320px under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.

Reuses `privacy.css` rather than adding a stylesheet. Linked from the shared footer, the home footer, `sitemap.ts` and `llms.txt`. `check-parity.mjs` untouched — its lists are a frozen legacy snapshot and its checks are presence-only.

## Review

Three cycles with `ui-ux-expert`, which **blocked once**: the copy claimed a sitewide manual keyboard pass that hadn't happened. Rather than soften the sentence, the pass was run. Each cycle caught one further overclaim on the same lines — a reduced-motion count that implied 9 stylesheets were all of them, a focus-ring baseline credited to tokens that define none, and an `aria-expanded` relocation described as universal when two call sites lose the attribute instead. All corrected.

Two apparent findings were discarded as artifacts of the measuring script rather than written into the page: "keyboard traps" on `/privacy` and `/accessibility` were the nine identical `#` heading anchors colliding in a string dedup key, and 142 "ring-less" nodes on `/architecture-map` were the SVG map nodes using the thickened `rect.box` stroke that `architecture-map.css:509` deliberately swaps in for `outline`.

## Follow-ups filed in `NEXT_ISSUES.md`

The `text-foreground/NN` ramp migration · the two landmark rules · **no permanent a11y gate for `apps/landing`** (every scan here ran from throwaway scripts under `apps/desktop/`, so nothing re-checks these pages on future changes) · the unscanned extension · PDF/UA-1 tagging.

title: ci: add a blocking accessibility gate for the landing site
body:
Follow-up to #924. That PR fixed every WCAG A/AA violation on the landing site and published `/accessibility`, a public page that **states those results**. Nothing re-checked them — so the fixes could regress silently and the statement would start lying. Every scan in #924 ran from throwaway scripts under `apps/desktop/`, the only place `@axe-core/playwright` already resolved. This makes it permanent.

## The gate

`apps/landing/scripts/check-a11y.mjs` serves the built `out/` with `node:http` (no server dep, mirroring `check-parity.mjs`), drives headless Chromium + axe-core, and scans **every route discovered by globbing `out/**/*.html`** — never a hardcoded list. A hardcoded list is the exact failure mode #924's review flagged, where a new route had to be added by hand in four separate places to be covered at all. Auto-discovery means a new page is covered the day it exists.

Tag set is `wcag2a/wcag2aa/wcag21a/wcag21aa/wcag22aa` — the same set `/accessibility`'s published numbers were measured with, deliberately not widened to best-practice rules.

**It blocks.** That differs from the three desktop a11y checks on purpose, and the file header says so in case someone later tries to harmonise it down:

| check | behaviour | why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `e2e/a11y.spec.ts` | logs, never fails | surface isn't clean yet |
| `eslint.a11y.config.mjs` | warn-only | surface isn't clean yet |
| `.lighthouserc.json` | warn assertion | surface isn't clean yet |
| **`check:a11y`** | **fails the build** | **baseline is 0 — anything found is a regression against a public claim** |

Runs on **pull requests**, inside the existing test job, reusing the Chromium already installed there for the Storybook vitest project. No new job. (Note `check:parity` runs only in `pages.yml` on push-to-main — post-merge, which would be too late for this.)

## What it found on its first run

Auto-discovery turned up **13 routes, not the 9** previously scanned. Three had never been checked:

- **`/404` and `/_not-found`** — clean.
- **`/mission-control`** — `color-contrast` at **4.03:1** on row-title links, 5 nodes. **Fixed.** `docs-tokens.css` already defines `--doc-accent-text` for exactly this case, and `.mc-badge.is-stale` documents the identical failure. Needed `.doc-shell .mc-row__title a` to out-specify the `.doc-shell a` base rule, which wins on source order because the page renders its own `<PageStyle>` before `DocShell`'s. Now **5.7:1**.
- **`/benchmarks/`** — `color-contrast` 3.15:1 on `#dl-button` plus a missing `lang` on `<html>`. **Excluded, not fixed** — it's generated by `benchmark-action` and overwritten wholesale by `quality.yml`'s `benchmark` job on every push-to-main perf run, so an in-repo edit would be reverted by CI. `EXCLUDED_ROUTES` names the generating workflow and both violations, and the gate **logs the exclusion** rather than skipping silently.

## Statement updated to match

A gate finding a barrier it can't fix is exactly the case `/accessibility` exists for, so the page discloses it rather than quietly keeping a clean number:

- "0 violations across all 9 pages" → **12 routes** the permanent gate covers, with `/404`, `/_not-found` and `/mission-control` named.
- `/mission-control`'s contrast failure added to the fixed-barriers list.
- New card disclosing `/benchmarks/` — a public page on the domain with two violations, excluded because it's third-party-generated. Stated as *excluded, not passing*.
- The gate added under "What's in place", explicitly contrasted as **blocking** against the three desktop checks — whose wording is untouched, because they didn't change.

**Every prior disclosure stands.** Both surfaces remain **partially conformant**; the extension is still *not assessed*; PDFs are still not PDF/UA-1 tagged; the desktop contrast fix is still scoped to the home view (~460 sub-AA `text-foreground/NN` usages elsewhere); still no third-party audit and no AT-user testing. No conformance verdict was upgraded — the `partially conformant` and never-`fully conformant` regression tests still pass.

## Proof the gate bites

A gate that can't fail is worse than no gate, so this was verified rather than assumed: lightening `--red` in `privacy.css` made it fail on both `/privacy` and `/accessibility` (which reuses that stylesheet) with exact selectors, fg/bg colours and measured-vs-required ratios, exit code 1. Reverted, back to green.

```
check:a11y — excluding 1 route(s) from the gate (see EXCLUDED_ROUTES): /benchmarks/
check:a11y OK — 12 page(s) scanned, 0 WCAG A/AA violations (1 page(s) excluded, see EXCLUDED_ROUTES).
```

`@axe-core/playwright` is declared explicitly in `apps/landing` rather than relying on `shamefullyHoist: true` — it resolves either way, but a gate's dependencies shouldn't hinge on a global pnpm setting.

## Cost note

The test job now also builds the landing static export. Chromium is already installed and cached there, so the added cost is the Next build. If that becomes a drag, the build output could be cached or the gate split into its own job.

title: feat: diagnose the role a cover letter answers before drafting it
body:
Folds a company-and-vacancy intelligence pass into the existing single-pass cover-letter generation. No extra AI calls, no new IPC, no new UI — the two research steps already had homes, only their content was thin.

## Company analysis
`commands/ai_provider/research.rs` — the opt-in "Research company" brief (provider-native web search: OpenAI / Anthropic / Gemini natively, Ollama via the Web Search API) now also covers **competitors** and the **challenges / strategic priorities the company is working on**, and carries a fact-vs-inference rule: state a fact plainly only when a search result supports it, hedge what was inferred, omit a facet rather than guess. Brief 120-150 → 150-200 words; the Ollama search query asks for competitors/strategy too.

`buildCompanyResearchBlock`'s fence cap moves 1200 → 1600 chars so the longer brief is not sliced mid-sentence.

## Vacancy analysis + matching
`cover-letter.ts` WRITING NOTES — a private diagnosis before drafting:

1. **why this role is open** — the business problem it exists to solve, read off the ad's own signals (what it repeats, what it lists first, scope, seniority, team, what "you will own") plus the brief when present
2. **the first 6 to 12 months** — the 3 outcomes the hire is judged on
3. **the through-line** — which real résumé achievements make the candidate part of that solution

Every step is bound to evidence in `<job_ad>`, `<company_research>`, or `<candidate_resume>`. Thin evidence keeps the diagnosis broad instead of guessing — an invented problem or piece of company news is worse than a general one — and the letter voices it as the candidate's own reading of the role, never insider knowledge. The "heart" movement now asks achievements to prove the candidate can solve that problem. The same one-liner goes into the agent-mode `draft_cover_letter` prompt.

The diagnosis names `<company_research>` only when a brief is actually fenced above; without one it runs on the ad + résumé alone.

## Drive-by
Drops the hardcoded "200 to 300 words" from four places — it contradicted `<market_conventions>`, which already carries the per-market band (intl 200-350, DE 250-400).

## Deliberately not done
- **No interactive 3-question intake** — the app already has company / JD / CV / country / language as structured inputs.
- **No second AI call for the vacancy analysis** — the model has the ad + brief in context; a round-trip buys latency, not insight. Worth adding only if the diagnosis should be *shown* to the user rather than only used.
- **No follow-up questions on missing evidence** — that needs a UI turn mid-generation; the prompt degrades to "keep it broad" instead.

`@ajh/prompts` 555 tests · `cargo test --lib` (research + agent::tools) · `pnpm typecheck` · `pnpm lint` · `cargo clippy --all-features` · `cargo fmt --check` · pre-push gate incl. AI review: clean.

title: fix: restore agent-fleet assembly-line scroll pin broken by doc-shell overflow
body:
## Problem

On the landing site's `/agent-system` page ("The Agent Fleet"), the **Assembly Line** section stopped pinning. It's built to pin to the viewport (`position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100vh`) while a `height: 340vh` runway scrolls past, so the conveyor belt scrubs horizontally as you scroll. Instead, the panel just scrolled away with the page.

## Root cause

Regression from **#742** (`774468eb`, the docs-tier / `DocShell` conversion), *not* the recent TSX PRs. That commit moved the page under the shared `DocShell` wrapper and put `overflow-x: hidden` on the `.doc-shell` **div** — whereas the old standalone `agent-system.html` had it on `<body>`.

- `overflow` on `<body>` propagates to the **viewport**, which stays the scroll container → `position: sticky` pins fine.
- `overflow-x: hidden` on an ordinary div forces the computed `overflow-y` to `auto` (CSS Overflow L3), making `.doc-shell` a **scroll container**. The sticky panel then resolves against `.doc-shell` — which grows with its content and never scrolls internally — so it has zero scroll range and never pins.

## Fix

Use `overflow-x: clip` on `.doc-shell`. `clip` clips horizontal overflow **without** establishing a scroll container, so descendant sticky pins resolve against the viewport again. A layered `overflow-x: hidden` fallback sits under it for engines without `clip` (Safari <16 / Chrome <90 / Firefox <81) — those keep today's clipping behavior (no regression); modern engines apply `clip` (last-valid-wins) and get the pin back. The repo has no `browserslist` baseline, hence the fallback.

```css
.doc-shell {
  …
  overflow-x: hidden; /* fallback for engines without overflow:clip */
  overflow-x: clip;   /* clip not hidden — hidden makes .doc-shell a scroll container and breaks sticky pins */
}
```

Reproduced and fixed in a live browser (Chrome, dev server):

| | `overflow-x: hidden` (before) | `overflow-x: clip` (after) |
|---|---|---|
| Sticky panel top vs viewport at mid-runway | **−1170px** (scrolled away) | **0px** (pinned) |
| Pinned across 0/25/50/75% of runway | no | **yes** |
| Computed `overflow-y` | `auto` (scroll container) | `visible` |
| Horizontal scrollbar | no | no (`scrollWidth === clientWidth`) |

Confirmed visually: belt pins and scrubs horizontally through the 9 stations with the diff chip riding along.

## Scope

One rule in `apps/landing/src/styles/doc-shell.css`. `frontend-reviewer`: APPROVE (no HIGH/CRITICAL). No other `DocShell`-wrapped route (`architecture-map`, `mission-control`) relies on `.doc-shell` scroll containment.

title: feat: revoke extension pairing over the bridge on token rotation
body:
After a factory reset (or Settings→Regenerate), the extension kept saying "authorized" while nothing worked — the token rotated silently, live sockets survived, and the extension retried the dead token forever. This adds a `token.revoked` protocol message: sent only over already-authenticated sessions right before rotation, then sockets close and the connected count zeroes; the extension clears its stored token and shows the pairing view. Reset confirm copy now says the browser must be paired again (en+de).

Security-hardened through three review rounds: the revoke handler is gated on an explicit post-serverProof `authenticated` flag (an unauthenticated port-squatter probing the between-handshake-steps window was empirically driven pre-fix and is pinned by a permanent probe test, 7-window matrix); no token material rides the frame; unauthenticated peers still get the silent no-oracle close; the rotation lock-ordering was adversarially verified (no interleaving authenticates on the old token and misses the revoke). Old published extensions ignore the new verb safely (unknown-type no-op, pinned).

**Release note / known limitation.** The revoke only reaches browsers that are LIVE at the moment of rotation. A browser that was closed (or whose MV3 service worker had been evicted) never receives the frame, so on its next launch it still retries the dead token and shows "app not running" rather than the pairing view — the user has to hit Unpair manually. This is inherent to the no-oracle design: the desktop cannot tell a stale-token reconnect from a crashed app without becoming a token oracle, which is exactly what ADR-0010 forbids. Follow-up (not in this PR): after N consecutive failed handshakes, have the extension surface a non-authoritative "still not connecting — re-pair?" hint.

Note: shipping the fix to users requires a Chrome Web Store + Firefox AMO re-release.
